senses.gloss: नासिका- + अग्र नासिका- + अग्र, n. the tip of the nose.
नष्ट-आतङ्क + म् नष्ट-आतङ्क + म्, adv. fearless, Śāk. d. 14 n.

1. नश् नश्, i. 1, Par. To attain (ved.).
 --Cf. Lat. nanciscor, and 2. नश्.

2. नश् नश् (the base of many forms is नंश्), i. 4, Par. (also Ātm., Rām. 5, 27, 24, and i. 1, Par. and Ātm., MBh. 13, 3083; 7, 685.),
 1. To be lost, Man. 8, 32.
 2. To disappear, Man. 8, 247.
 3. To escape, MBh. 5, 2736.
 4. To go away, Rām. 5, 27, 24.
 5. To perish, Man. 4, 52.
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. नष्ट,
 1. Lost, Śāk. d. 167.
 2. Invisible, Rām. 3, 50, 7; disappeared, MBh. 3, 2690.
 3. Destroyed, MBh. 1, 3147.
 4. Dead, Man. 8, 166.
 --Caus. नाशय,
 1. To cause to disappear, Rām. 1, 55, 20.
 2. To efface, Man. 11, 245.
 3. To destroy, Rām. 5, 63, 8; Man. 2, 55.
 4. To violate, Daśak. in Chr. 191, 10.
 5. To extinguish, Bhāg. P. 4, 5, 20.
 6. To lose, Pañc. i. d. 23.
 7. To disappear, MBh. 5, 862.
 --With the prep. व्यप वि-अप, Caus. To remove, MBh. 5, 7090.
 --With अव अव, To disappear, 4, 1728.
 --With निस् निस्, निर्नष्ट, Disappeared, Rājat. 1, 83. []
 --With प्र प्र णश् णश्, except where ś is changed to ष्, e. g. प्र-नष्ट,
 1. To be lost, Man. 8, 149.
 2. To disappear, Bhag. 1, 40. प्रनष्ट (sometimes erroneously प्रणष्ट),
 1. Perished, Rājat. 5, 211.
 2. Disappeared, Man. 8, 30.
 3. Escaped, Pañc. 89, 20.
 --Caus.
 1. To cause to disappear, MBh. 7, 327.
 2. To cause to be lost, Hit. iv. d. 9 (to leave unrewarded).
 --With विप्र वि-प्र,
 1. To disappear, MBh. 3, 5027.
 2. To be lost, 13, 3212. विप्रनष्ट,
 1. Disappeared, MBh. 4, 877.
 2. Lost, 1, 4802.
 --With संप्र सम्-प्र, To be lost, MBh. 3, 13781. सम्प्रनष्ट, Disappeared, 2847.
 --With वि वि,
 1. To disappear, Man. 11, 263.
 2. To perish, 2, 163. विनष्ट,
 1. Lost, Mālav. 9, 3.
 2. Utterly ruined or spoiled, Man. 7, 41; 2, 64.
 --Caus.
 1. To destroy, 7, 19.
 2. To kill, Pañc. 71, 24.
 3. To perish (Aor.), Rām. 2, 110, 30.
 --Desid. of the Caus. विनाशयिषित, without reduplication; read rather निनाश्˚, Sought to be destroyed, Daśak. 112, 3, below.
 --With अनुवि अनु-वि, To perish afterward, or together with, MBh. 12, 3400.
 --With प्रवि प्र-वि, To perish, Rām. 1, 56, 27 Gorr.
 --With सम् सम्, संनष्ट, Perished, Rām. 5, 51, 13.
 --Cf. 1. नश्, The original signification of 1. and 2. नश्, has been probably, To hasten (cf. Lat. per-nix); then on the one side, To overtake, to attain (1. नश्); on the other, To hasten out of view, to disappear, to vanish, to perish (2. नश्).
 --Cf. νέκυς, νεκρός, etc.; Lat. per-nicies, necare, nocere, ve-nenum (for ve-nec + num); Goth. naus (for nahu + s = νέκυς), navis.

नस् नस्, i. 1, Ātm.
 1. † To be crooked.
 2. To go to, to join (ved.).
 --Cf. νέομαι (? perhaps = ved. नु), νίσσομαι (for νεσϳομαι), νόστος.
नस् नस् see नासा and अस्मद्.
† नास् नास्, i. 1, Ātm. To sound.

नश्वर 2. नश् + वर, adj., f. री, [] Perishable, Kathās. 19, 50.
 --Comp.
नश्वरत्व नश्वर + त्व, n. Perishableness, Daśak. in Chr. 185, 15.
नष्टि नष्टि, i. e. नश् + ति, f. Ruin, Bhāg. P. 9, 10, 21.

ऽनस -नस् + अ, a substitute for नासा, when latter part of a comp. adj., e. g. उन्नस, i. e. उद्-, adj. Having a prominent nose, Bhāg. P. 8, 8, 42. गो-,
 1. m. A large kind of snake, Suśr. 2, 265, 12.
 2. f. सा, The nose of a cow, 2, 171, 7.
 3. f. सी, A certain plant, 2, 170, 1. वि-, adj. Noseless. सु-, adj. Handsomenosed.

नाश नाश, i. e. 2. नश् + अ, m.
 1. Loss, Bhartṛ. 2, 35.
 2. Disappearance, Rām. 2, 47, 13.
 3. Destruction, Yājñ. 1, 339.
 4. Death, 63.
 --Comp.

नासा नासा, the base of some cases and derivatives is नस्, f. The nose, Man. 8, 125.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. O.H.G. nasa; A.S. nase; Lat. nâsus, nâris.
नस्तक नस् + त + क, m. A hole bored through the bridge of the nose of cattle for draught, MBh. 12, 9377.
नस्ततस् नस् + त + तस्, adv. Out of the nose, MBh. 4, 2227.

नस्तस् नस् + तस्, adv.
 1. Out of the nose, Bhāg. P. 2, 7, 11.
 2. In the nose, Suśr. 2, 297, 6.

नस्य नस् + य, n.
 1. A sternutatory, Suśr. 2, 235, 21. 2. f. या, A nosebridle.
 --Comp.

नास्य नास्य, i. e. नासा + य, n.
 1. A nose-cord, Man. 8, 291.
 2. A multitude of noses (?), Hariv. 15996.

नस्योत नस्योत, i. e. नस् + इ-आ-उत (vb. वे), adj.
 1. Led by a string through the septum of the nose, MBh. 3, 1142.

नाशक नाशक, i. e. 2. नश्, Caus., + अक, adj. Destroying, MBh. 13, 1634.
 --Comp.

नाशन नाशन, i. e. 2. नश्, Caus., + अन,
 I. adj., f. नी
 1. Destroying, MBh. 13, 2194; Man. 8, 127.
 2. Removing, MBh. 2, 426.
 II. n.
 1. Destruction, Mārk. P. 24, 36.
 2. Removal, MBh. 7, 5120.
 --Comp.

नाशिन् नाशिन्, i. e. 2. नश्, or नाश + इन्, adj., f. नी,
 1. Perishable, Prab. 100, 11.
 2. Removing, Hariv. 10239.
 3. Destroying, Rām. 6, 80, 32.
 --Comp.
नाष्टिक नाष्टिक, i. e. नष्ट (vb. 2. नश्) + इक, m. The former owner who has lost a chattel.

नासत्य नासत्य, i. e. न-अ-सत्य,
 I. m. du. A name of the Aśvins, MBh. 12, 7583.
 II. adj. Referring to the Nāsatyas, 12, 13491.

नासिका नासिका, i. e. नासा + क, f.
 1. A nostril, Bhāg. P. 5, 23, 6.
 2. du. The nose, 2, 10, 20.
 3. sing. The nose, Man. 2, 90.
 4. The trunk of an elephant, MBh. 13, 4900.
 --Comp.
नास्तिक नास्तिक, i. e. न-अस्ति (vb. 1. अस्) + क, m. An unbeliever, Man. 2, 11.
नास्तिकता नास्तिक + ता, f. Infidelity, MBh. 12, 4539.

नास्तिक्य नास्तिक्य, i. e. नास्तिक + य,
 1. Disbelief, Man. 3, 65.
 2. Infidelity, 4, 163.
नासा-रक्त- + पित्त नासा-रक्त- + पित्त, n. bleeding of the nose.
नासा- + पुट नासा- + पुट, m. the nostril.
नष्ट- + रूप नष्ट- + रूप, adj. disappeared, MBh. 3, 2604.
नासा- + वंश नासा- + वंश, [] m. the bone of the nose, Pañc. 182, 16 (at the end of a comp. adj.).
नासा- + विवर नासा- + विवर, n. the nostril, ib. 3, 15, 18.
न- + संविद् न- + संविद्, f. want of consciousness, Bhartṛ. 1, 27, v. r.
नासा- + स्राव नासा- + स्राव, m. catarrh, Suśr. 2, 371, 14.
